subject: Orca Industrial SIG - Control Evidence Sequencing & Escalation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@orcaindustrial.com>, ORCA Security Team <security@orcaindustrial.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Orca Industrial SIG - Control Evidence Sequencing & Escalation

Hi Samantha / Orca security team,

Thanks again for the SIG intake yesterday. To keep momentum, we put together a proposed sequencing for evidence delivery so your procurement and security reviewers can get the highest-risk controls first. Attached is a control_mapping.xlsx with our suggested ordering and requested artifact types (attestation, log sample, configuration screenshot, or full export).

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm which controls must have raw artifacts vs. an engineer attestation?
- For privileged access controls (CC6.x), please confirm whether you need 90 days of logs or a 30-day sample for initial review.
- If there are any third-party attestations you require (e.g., downstream DB hosting provider), flag them in an email so we can coordinate.

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- Day 0–3: Priority controls (authentication, encryption, privileged access)
- Day 4–7: Infrastructure and change management artifacts
- Day 8–14: Remaining controls + remediations / clarifications

I copied Lauren to coordinate collection and Stephanie for technical artifacts. We can escalate to our compliance team if you require vendor-specific documentation for Private deployments.

Attachments: control_mapping.xlsx (mapping + requested artifact type)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@orcaindustrial.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: ORCA Security Team <security@orcaindustrial.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@orcaindustrial.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orca Industrial SIG - Control Evidence Sequencing & Escalation

Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the mapping. This looks helpful. A few notes from our side:

- Priorities: Please treat CC6.1 (privileged access provisioning) and CC6.3 (session recording) as highest priority — our internal auditors will want either 90 days of logs or a 30-day rolling sample plus a control narrative.
- Attestations: For infra-level controls we can accept engineer attestations initially, but production encryption keys (CC9.x) will require key-management screenshots and the KMS policy excerpt.
- Vendor exceptions: The database provider is currently on our approved list; no additional vendor attestations required for now.

Uploading our prioritization csv to the Drive link you shared and attaching a copy here for your intake.

Attachments: priority_controls.csv

We can do a 30-minute sync Thu 16 Feb at 10:00 PT if that works for your team.

—Samantha
Samantha Price
Procurement Manager | Orca Industrial
samantha.price@orcaindustrial.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Orca Industrial SIG - Control Evidence Sequencing & Escalation

All — I'm taking point on collection. Notes from Ben/Samantha above: prioritize CC6.1/6.3 and CC9.x. Action items:

- Stephanie: prepare initial SOC2 evidence bundle (config exports + screenshots) for CC9.x and CC6.*. Zip and place in shared Drive under /Orca/InitialBundle.
- Rishi: draft the compliance narrative for privileged access and confirm whether we can provide a 30-day sample for the first pass.
- Ben: keep procurement PO/terms conversation on the thread; they hinted at a PO requirement later in process.

Target delivery: send initial bundle by end of day Thu 16 Feb (to match the proposed sync). I will triage follow-ups during the call.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@orcaindustrial.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 09:58:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Orca Industrial SIG - initial evidence bundle

Hi Samantha — attaching the initial evidence bundle per Lauren's plan. Contents include:

- SOC2-evidence-bundle.zip (config exports, control narratives, screenshots)
- access-logs-sample.csv (30-day sample of privileged session logs)
- control_mapping.xlsx (updated with flags for redaction items)

A couple of implementation notes:
- We redacted IP addresses of internal infra in screenshots; let us know if you need unredacted entries under an NDA.
- The access log is a sample exported from our audit service and includes column headers and anonymized user IDs; if you need raw user identifiers for correlation, we will request additional approval.
- For CC9.x key management artifacts, we included KMS policy excerpts and screenshots from the control plane; the full KMS audit trail is available on request.

If the bundle looks good, we'll add full exports for any controls you mark as high priority.

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-bundle.zip, access-logs-sample.csv

Subject: Escalation: additional attestation request for CC6.2 (privileged session tamper-resistance)

Samantha — following up from our sync this morning. You flagged CC6.2 as requiring extra validation that session recordings are tamper-evident for on-prem connectors. We can provide two routes:

1) Operational proof: additional hashed audit exports and a KMS-signed manifest demonstrating immutability (we can produce this within 5 business days).
2) Architecture route: for customers with strict requirements we have a Private deployment package with HSM-backed key storage and extended audit retention. I attached a short compliance note for the Private option.

Given procurement timelines you mentioned, option 1 is likely the fastest. If you need the Private package, we'll involve our Legal/Enterprise team for licensing and an SLA amendment.

Forwarding Samantha's note for context:

Confirming the 30-minute follow-up on Mon 20 Feb at 10:00 PT to review the manifest and outstanding items. Also, procurement flagged that they will need a simple procurement timeline and PO requirements — attaching our internal procurement timeline for reference.

Attachments: procurement-timelines.pdf

Appreciate the quick responses from the team.
